decisions.reason: As a standard rye bread close to the core assortment, it is cheap to continue and there is not enough negative evidence yet to justify abandoning the option.
The gold medal is a strong positive signal for this premium seasonal product, so uncertainty is lower and keeping it is clearly worthwhile.
This seeded rye mixed bread fits existing capabilities well, and although it overlaps with other breads, the cost of keeping it while demand becomes clearer is still modest.
This darker malted rye variant is somewhat more niche and faces overlap within the bread range, but it still uses familiar processes so management would likely keep the option open for now.
A marzipan stollen is a natural adjacent seasonal offer for a German bakery, and without clear signs of weak acceptance it is sensible to retain it for another season.
The ancient grain bread is a more novel extension with uncertain demand, but its strategic upside and manageable continuation cost argue for further market testing rather than immediate withdrawal.
